ledger.claim: The trip deviated, and the deviation is established under POL-RD-01 on the trace figure, which governs. The trace records 9.56 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event; the platform optimal stored on the trip record at booking is 7.4 km. Excess = 2.16 km and 29.19% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trip record's actual_distance_km of 9.6 is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is deliberately not relied on for the threshold test.

The excess stands on the trace alone. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 130 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gap between consecutive fixes above 10 seconds, the largest straight-line step between consecutive fixes 122.3 m, and the highest implied speed 44.0 km/h. None of limbs (a), (b) or (c) of POL-RD-07 is met, so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

No external-traffic exoneration is available to reduce this excess. The only traffic-advisory artifact in the bundle is EV-ADVIS-04001-01, which is MISSING: it has no payload and carries weight 0.0. There is accordingly no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, matched by a route leaving and re-joining the optimal corridor, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The driver's statement does not assert a traffic cause at all; had one been asserted, POL-RD-13 would discard it for want of the advisory record.

ledger.claim: The chat log is IMPAIRED: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY (MSG-04001-002 mixes Malay 'singgah' and 'kejap' with English), and I disclose that discount. What it shows is a request for a stop, not a request for a route: 'later can singgah Jurong Point kejap? need to collect parcel at the POPStation, 3 min only', answered by the driver 'ok can, I drop you at the taxi stand side'. Under POL-RD-04 only the excess distance between leaving and re-joining the optimal corridor is excluded; the rider never authorised 2.16 km of additional driving, and the driver's account of what happened cites no evidence ID in his statement, so under POL-RD-08 that assertion carries no weight and is discarded.

The quantum of any POL-RD-04 exclusion is not on this record and must not be invented. The waypoint_approach block reports only the nearest fix to the requested waypoint — 49.8 m, at 10:18:02 — and nothing in the bundle identifies where the vehicle left the optimal corridor or where it re-joined it. With no measured leave-and-rejoin stretch, the excess cannot be adjusted down on the evidence as it stands, and the figure that governs POL-RD-02 remains the measured 2.16 km against the booked optimal of 7.4 km.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. The fare model on the fare breakdown is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs (not POL-RD-11), and the surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0. Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.4 + 0.28 x 15) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge - 0 promo discount = 13.55 + 0.80 = 14.35. Charged total is 17.65, so the refund is 17.65 - 14.35 = 3.30. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis (so the outcome is not NO_ACTION) and is 18.7% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome for the filing rider is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.30, rounded up to the nearest 0.05.

Nothing is added on top of that figure and nothing is double-counted. The fare breakdown's ERP block shows on-optimal-route total 0.00 and off-optimal-route total 0.00 with no gantry lines, there is no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates nor terminates at an airport), and the waiting-time fee is 0.00, so the POL-RD-09 pass-through correction is nil and the distance-and-time refund of 3.30 stands alone as the entire monetary correction.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case can be ruled on. The trip identifier matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the timestamps are consistent and causally ordered, with the trace's first fix equal to started_at 10:12:40 and its last fix equal to ended_at 10:33:55; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); every charge line has a counterpart on the record; and the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total.

Confidence is not capped below the platform floor. The artifacts that carry the deciding facts — the trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 escalation floor is not reached; the only impaired artifact on the bundle is the chat log at 0.85 with issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, and it does not carry the deciding fact of the measured excess.

The detour the rider now disputes is one the rider herself ordered. MSG-04001-002 in EV-CHAT-04001 was sent by the RIDER at 10:11:40 and reads 'uncle later can singgah Jurong Point kejap? need to collect parcel at the POPStation, 3 min only'; it carries waypoint_hint Jurong Point (1.33975, 103.7064), which the platform itself resolved from the message text at ingest. That satisfies POL-RD-04(a), the instruction comes from the rider, and POL-RD-04(c), it identifies a place specifically enough to act on. It is not one of the vague messages the clause excludes. EV-CHAT-04001 is impaired and I disclose it rather than present it as clean: admissibility status IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.85, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, because MSG-04001-002 mixes Malay ('singgah', 'kejap') with English. Even at that discount the artifact sits well above the platform's 0.70 confidence floor, and the driver's acceptance, MSG-04001-003, is in plain English.

The instruction came before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, which is what POL-RD-04(b) requires. MSG-04001-002 was sent at 10:11:40; the trip did not start until 10:12:40, when the rider came on board (EV-TRIP-04001, trip_started event); and even the driver's assent, MSG-04001-003, was sent at 10:12:00, still before departure. The vehicle therefore left the corridor on the rider's instruction and not on the driver's own initiative. (EV-CHAT-04001 carries the impairment disclosed above: IMPAIRED, weight 0.85, LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY.)

POL-RD-04's corroboration test is satisfied on the platform's own computation. Fix 33 of EV-GPS-04001, at 10:18:02, lies 49.83 m from the requested waypoint - well inside the clause's 200 m threshold - so the vehicle did pass within 200 m of the place the rider named, exactly as POL-RD-04 demands. The geometry comes from EV-GPS-04001, a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0 (130 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gaps); the instruction it corroborates comes from EV-CHAT-04001, impaired at 0.85 for LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, which I disclose.

The stop actually happened, and the rider's own messages say so. She asked for three minutes (MSG-04001-002), and at 10:20:45 she sent MSG-04001-004: 'ok got it, coming back to the car now'. That sentence only makes sense if she had left the vehicle at the requested stop and was returning to it. The driver's account - he waited at the taxi stand about three minutes and then drove on to Bukit Batok - matches both the chat and the trace. (EV-CHAT-04001 is impaired: IMPAIRED, weight 0.85, LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY.)

Because the detour was rider-requested and corroborated, POL-RD-04 excludes the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor 'before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied', and on this record that is the whole of the measured excess. The platform's own derived deviation is 2.16 km, or 29.19%, against the 7.4 km booked optimal - above the 0.8 km and 20% establishment gates of POL-RD-01 but far below its 8.0 km and 50% materiality gates, so POL-RD-06 never engages. The rider's own narrative describes a single loop ('one big round'), the only stop the record contains is the Jurong Point waypoint the trace approaches, and nothing in the evidence identifies any second departure from the corridor. Exclude that excess and no deviation survives POL-RD-01, no refund arithmetic under POL-RD-02 is reached, and the rider's claim fails.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 3.3, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 2 (sampled): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 3 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 3.3, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 4 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
